subject: Materials Science
title: Carbon Nanotubes: Tiny Cylinders of Strength
description: A quick, practical guide to Carbon Nanotubes: Tiny Cylinders of Strength.

hook.text: A tube of rolled graphene — 100 times stronger than steel at one-sixth the weight. The carbon nanotube.

buildup.text: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are seamless cylinders of sp² carbon — single-walled (1 nm) or multi-walled (5–50 nm).

discovery.text: Their chirality — how the graphene sheet is rolled — determines whether the tube is metallic or semiconducting.

twist.text: Making all CNTs the same chirality is extremely hard — mixed metallic and semiconducting tubes limit use.

climax.text: CNTs reinforce composites, conduct electricity in flexible screens, and carry drugs into cancer cells.

punchline.text: Roll atoms into a tube — the strongest, most conductive fiber ever made.

quiz.question: What determines whether a carbon nanotube is metallic or semiconducting?
options: Its chirality — the angle at which the graphene sheet is rolled
The temperature at which it was grown
